messages.Under 21 CFR 101.93(a), the manufacturer: Under 21 CFR 101.93(a), the manufacturer, packer, or distributor of a dietary supplement that bears a structure/function, general well-being, or nutrient-deficiency claim must notify FDA no later than 30 days after the first marketing of the supplement. The notification must include the firm's name and address, the text of the statement, the name of the dietary ingredient, and the name of the supplement.
messages.Under 21 CFR 101.93(c) through (e), the: Under 21 CFR 101.93(c) through (e), the disclaimer must be prominently displayed in boldface type in letters no smaller than one-sixteenth inch, placed adjacent to the statement with no intervening material, or linked to the statement with a symbol such as an asterisk. Multiple claims may share one plural disclaimer under the same placement rules.
messages.Under 21 CFR 111.70, manufacturers must: Under 21 CFR 111.70, manufacturers must establish specifications for identity, purity, strength, and composition of components and finished products, and verify that they are met.
messages.Under 21 CFR Part 111 Subpart O, a quali: Under 21 CFR Part 111 Subpart O, a qualified person must review all product complaints to decide whether they involve a possible failure of a dietary supplement to meet any specification or a possible risk of illness or injury, and certain complaints must be investigated with a written record. The rule is written for dietary supplement manufacturers, packers, and holders rather than for every upstream ingredient maker. FDA's Small Entity Compliance Guide states that a manufacturer of dietary ingredients that does not sell directly to consumers is not subject to the Part 111 product-complaint requirements in the same way, but FDA recommends sharing complaint information through the manufacturing chain so others can take corrective action.
messages.Under 21 CFR part 111 subpart O, supplem: Under 21 CFR part 111 subpart O, supplement manufacturers must maintain written procedures for product complaints, review all complaints for possible specification failures, investigate complaints that could involve a risk of illness or injury, and keep a written record of each complaint with lot number, date, nature, reply, and findings. A buyer should expect the supplier to document complaints this way and to extend the review to all relevant batches.
messages.Under 21 CFR Part 111, manufacturers mus: Under 21 CFR Part 111, manufacturers must establish specifications for components and finished products, including identity, purity, strength, and composition, and verify they are met.
messages.Under 7 CFR 205.100, an operation that p: Under 7 CFR 205.100, an operation that produces or handles agricultural products sold, labeled, or represented as "100 percent organic", "organic", or "made with organic" must be certified by an accredited certifying agent. A supplier selling "organic PS" should therefore hold current NOP certification naming the product in scope.
messages.Under 7 CFR 205.303, a packaged product: Under 7 CFR 205.303, a packaged product labeled "organic" must identify each organic ingredient in the ingredient statement, show the percentage of organic ingredients where applicable, and identify the certifying agent of the finished-product handler. The USDA seal may be used only by certified operations, so the label requires certifier information the PS certificate must support.
messages.Under a C-rule such as CIP, the seller c: Under a C-rule such as CIP, the seller can pay carriage to a European destination even though risk transfers much earlier when the goods are handed to the first carrier. Under DAP, the seller pays carriage and retains transport risk to the named destination.
messages.Under Article 30 of Regulation (EU) 2018: Under Article 30 of Regulation (EU) 2018/848, organic terms may be used in the sales description of a processed food only when at least 95% of the agricultural ingredients by weight are organic; below that, organic terms may appear only in the ingredient list. For PS, the consequence is direct: non-certified PS blocks an "organic" sales description, because it counts against the 95% threshold and is not on the authorized non-organic list.
messages.Under Article 56 of Regulation 2017/625,: Under Article 56 of Regulation 2017/625, the operator uses the CHED to give prior notification to the border control post and submits the relevant part in IMSOC before physical arrival. Implementing Regulation 2019/1013 sets the normal minimum at one working day before expected arrival. Where transport logistics prevent that timing, the competent authority may apply a minimum of four hours. Importers should not plan around the exception; confirm the local BCP cut-off and submit when the shipment data is stable.
messages.Under CIP, does the seller carry risk un: Under CIP, does the seller carry risk until the PS arrives in Europe?
messages.Under CIP, the seller contracts and pays: Under CIP, the seller contracts and pays carriage to the named destination and arranges the required cargo insurance. The buyer handles import clearance. The frequent misunderstanding is the risk point: the seller's cost runs to the destination, but risk transfers when the goods are delivered to the first carrier.
messages.Under DAP, the seller delivers the goods: Under DAP, the seller delivers the goods to the named destination on the arriving means of transport, ready for unloading. The seller carries transport risk to that point. The buyer unloads and completes import formalities.
messages.Under FCA, the seller completes export f: Under FCA, the seller completes export formalities and delivers the goods to the buyer's carrier or nominated person at the agreed place. If delivery is at the seller's premises, the precise loading obligation differs from delivery at another location, so the wording needs attention.
messages.Under FDA dietary supplement GMPs, only: Under FDA dietary supplement GMPs, only after establishing the reliability of the supplier's results through qualification, confirmed at scheduled intervals. Identity generally cannot rely on the CoA alone. EU importers face parallel expectations.
messages.Under FSVP, importers must evaluate fore: Under FSVP, importers must evaluate foreign supplier performance, including whether the supplier is the subject of an FDA warning letter, import alert, or other compliance action, and document the evaluation. The same discipline is good practice for any buyer approving a supplier.

Confirm the exact formulation, moisture profile, and shipping conditions in writing with the supplier, and treat any doubt as a reason to apply the full checks.
messages.Under Regulation (EU) 2015/2283, food co: Under Regulation (EU) 2015/2283, food consisting of, isolated from, or produced from engineered nanomaterials is a novel food category, so a deliberately engineered nanoscale PS would need an authorization pathway, not just a specification row.
messages.Under Regulation (EU) 2018/848, organic: Under Regulation (EU) 2018/848, organic terms in the sales description require at least 95% of agricultural ingredients by weight to be organic, and non-organic agricultural ingredients may be used only if authorized. PS is not on the authorized list, so it would need certification.
messages.Under Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, the: Under Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, the date of minimum durability is a mandatory food-information particular, and special storage conditions or conditions of use are mandatory as well. In practice, the date is the period until which the product retains its specific properties when properly stored, and it must be supported by stability evidence that the finished product meets its specification throughout the declared period.

messages.Under Section 3 of the Act, CBP applies: Under Section 3 of the Act, CBP applies a statutory presumption that any goods mined, produced, or manufactured wholly or in part in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region (XUAR) of China, or produced by an entity actively listed on the UFLPA Entity List, are inherently prohibited from importation into the United States. This prohibition is enforced under Section 307 of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1307), which prohibits the entry of goods produced, wholly or in part, with forced labor. When the presumption is triggered, the goods are not entitled to entry and will be detained at the U.S. port of arrival.
messages.Under section 402 of the Federal Food, D: Under section 402 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, food is adulterated if it contains a poisonous or deleterious substance that may render it injurious to health. In the absence of a numeric MOSH/MOAH limit, FDA enforcement relies on that standard, which is why document-based supplier control is the practical tool.
messages.Under sections 201(s) and 409 of the Fed: Under sections 201(s) and 409 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and FDA’s implementing regulations, an intentionally added food substance generally requires food-additive authorization unless its use is GRAS or another exception applies. FDA explains that scientific-procedure GRAS conclusions require the same quantity and quality of scientific evidence as food-additive approval, plus general recognition among qualified experts.

messages.Under the bills, a change to information: Under the bills, a change to information on the label of an already-listed product would need to be submitted within 30 days after the changed product is first introduced into interstate commerce. Source-route, spec, formula, or manufacturing-site changes should therefore be evaluated as potential listing updates, which is why buyer-side change control matters.
messages.Under the bills, the listing would inclu: Under the bills, the listing would include product name and identity, responsible-person and U.S. agent information, an electronic label copy, all ingredients and amounts per serving, servings per container, directions for use, allergen statements, product form, claims on the label, and an FDA-assigned listing number.
messages.Under the bills, the responsible person: Under the bills, the responsible person is the manufacturer, packer, or distributor whose name appears on the label under FD&C Act section 403(e)(1). If that party is a foreign entity, a U.S. agent would submit the listing. For most U.S. supplement brands and private-label buyers, that means the brand or importer of record is the responsible person, not the bulk ingredient manufacturer. The manufacturer is the data source behind the listing.
messages.Under the Directive, a \"product\" is an: Under the Directive, a "product" is any movable item, including items integrated into or interconnected with another movable or immovable item. A food supplement containing phosphatidylserine is a movable product, and the ingredient itself - the PS powder in a 25 kg drum - is also one. The Directive does not carve food out of its scope; processed foods such as supplements have been covered by EU product liability rules for decades, and the new regime continues that coverage while broadening what counts as compensable damage.
messages.Under the Directive's role structure, th: Under the Directive's role structure, the EU-established importer is a liable operator on the same footing when the manufacturer is based outside the EU. If the importer also brands the finished supplement, it is additionally treated as the apparent manufacturer for that product.
messages.Under the proposal, any person introduci: Under the proposal, any person introducing a substance into interstate commerce under the GRAS provision of the FD&C Act would need to notify FDA of the basis for the GRAS conclusion, unless an exception applies.
messages.Under the rule, a shipper is a person, s: Under the rule, a shipper is a person, such as the manufacturer or a freight broker, who arranges for the transportation of food in the United States by one or more carriers. For an imported PS order, that can point to more than one company on the same shipment.
messages.Under the US Food Allergen Labeling and: Under the US Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act, soy is a major allergen that must be declared on supplement labels — typically as "contains soy." There is no de minimis threshold; presence triggers declaration. Sunflower is not a major allergen in the US or EU, so sunflower-derived PS carries no mandatory allergen statement. In the EU, Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 Annex II lists soybeans among the 14 mandatory allergens; sunflower is absent — the same origin choice satisfies both regimes.
messages.Under the US Uniform Commercial Code, Ar: Under the US Uniform Commercial Code, Article 2 governs transactions in goods; a PO that names product, quantity, price, and delivery creates the enforceable baseline quality and finance use later.
messages.Under U.S. customs rules, imported-merch: Under U.S. customs rules, imported-merchandise invoices must contain required information, and even simplified entry documentation still requires an adequate description, quantities, and values or approximate values. The practical implication is clear: "sample for testing" is not enough by itself if it hides what the material actually is.
messages.Under US dietary supplement GMP the fini: Under US dietary supplement GMP the finished-product manufacturer carries supplier qualification and incoming-testing obligations; under EU general food law the operator carries traceability one step back and one forward, with hygiene requirements set by Regulation (EC) No 852/2004. Also request an allergen statement, GMO status where relevant to the source, residual solvent and irradiation statements, and a completed supplier questionnaire covering change control, complaints, and recall procedure.

messages.US buyers often assume a GRAS determinat: US buyers often assume a GRAS determination or a completed NDI notification travels with the ingredient. It does not. The US framework evaluates safety under US law and definitions; the EU framework runs on its own cutoff date, its own Union list, and its own assessment criteria. A material can be lawfully marketed in the US and still require an EU authorization or notification pathway — and vice versa. When sourcing from a US-facing supplier for EU distribution, ask specifically about EU status evidence. Suppliers who sell meaningfully into Europe will have it; suppliers who have never shipped to the EU typically will not.

messages.Validation starts with a specification,: Validation starts with a specification, and the specification must come from the ingredient's stability behavior. For PS raw material, typical supplier storage recommendations are cool and dry — commonly 15–25 °C with low humidity, protected from light and oxygen — with the real constraint being cumulative heat exposure over the journey rather than any single reading. Work from three inputs: the supplier's recommended storage condition and shelf-life claim, your stability data (or the supplier's) showing behavior at accelerated conditions, and the finished-product dosage form's own sensitivities (softgels and gummies soften at lower temperatures than powders). The output is a written transport temperature profile: e.g., "maintain mean kinetic temperature below 25 °C; no more than 72 cumulative hours above 30 °C per shipment." messages.When a supplier sends a change notice, f: When a supplier sends a change notice, first record the current approved state: source, grade, site, process, specification, package, test method, and document revision. Then describe the proposed state and the reason for the change. A clear comparison lets the buyer decide whether the change is administrative, commercial, logistical, technical, regulatory, or potentially safety-relevant instead of treating every notice as equivalent.
messages.When a U.S. importer, distributor, or wa: When a U.S. importer, distributor, or warehouse address appears on the drum, 19 CFR 134.22(c) requires origin marking in close proximity to that U.S. address so the contents' origin is clear. The CBP marking rules in Subpart E also state that when U.S. wording or another non-origin location could mislead the ultimate purchaser, the actual country of origin must appear legibly and permanently in close proximity and in comparable size, preceded by wording such as "Made in" or "Product of."

messages.When particles partially dissolve at the: When particles partially dissolve at their surface and re-crystallize, they fuse into lumps. Higher moisture or water activity means a higher tendency to cake, which affects scooping, weighing, blending, and capsule filling.

messages.When procurement compares SSP samples, f: When procurement compares SSP samples, formulation teams should remove avoidable bias. Store both samples under the same conditions, acclimate them for the same period, and prepare them with the same water, batch size, vessels, mixer geometry, operator sequence, and measurement schedule. Randomise sample codes when practical so visual and sensory expectations do not drive the decision.
messages.When PS is used as an ingredient in food: When PS is used as an ingredient in food covered by the preventive controls rule, the receiving facility must establish a written, risk-based supply-chain program with approved suppliers, appropriate supplier verification activities, and documented verification (21 CFR 117.405 through 117.430). Verification activities can include onsite audits, sampling and testing, and review of the supplier's relevant food safety records. Where a hazard controlled by the supplier could result in serious adverse health consequences, an onsite audit is generally required before use and at least annually.
messages.When PS is used in foods covered by the: When PS is used in foods covered by the preventive-controls rule, 21 CFR 117.150 requires written corrective-action procedures where preventive controls are not properly implemented, including steps to identify and correct the problem, reduce the likelihood of recurrence, evaluate affected food, and keep affected food out of commerce when safety cannot be assured. Section 117.165 then requires verification that preventive controls are consistently implemented and effective.

messages.Within the European Union, Directive 201: Within the European Union, Directive 2011/7/EU on combating late payment sets the baseline for business-to-business payment periods: as a general rule, contractual payment periods are limited to 60 calendar days, with longer periods possible only if not grossly unfair to the creditor. Public authorities face a stricter norm: normally 30 days, at most 60. The directive also explicitly allows instalment payments. Two consequences matter for an importer: it governs payments inside the EU, not your contract with a supplier in China, so it does not cap the advance a Chinese supplier requests; and it shapes the terms your own EU customers expect, so your import schedule should be planned against your resale terms rather than funding a long customer window with a full advance.

Annual tenders should also ask for a volume-banded schedule and a variance mechanism, since a price that collapses when offtake runs below forecast triggers renegotiation by month four.

messages.Yes, an EORI is mandatory for customs-cl: Yes, an EORI is mandatory for customs-clearance operations in the EU. The team should confirm which operator owns the EORI and how the importer, declarant, consignee, and customs representative fit the declaration structure before dispatch.

messages.Yes, as a matter of control. The specifi: Yes, as a matter of control. The specification version defines what the COA is measured against and what receiving can accept. messages.Yes, at the packaging level. Maine restr: Yes, at the packaging level. Maine restricts food packaging with intentionally introduced PFAS above incidental presence and requires certificates of compliance; California restricts plant-based food packaging containing regulated PFAS, defined as intentionally added PFAS or presence at or above 100 ppm total organic fluorine. The drum liner and food-contact components are the units to check.
messages.Yes, but only with a complete file. CBP: Yes, but only with a complete file. CBP requires the importer to show the first sale was a bona fide arm's-length sale, the goods were clearly destined for the United States, and the price was settled in good faith (Nissho Iwai; CBP ruling H347879).
messages.Yes, buyers should perform soy-allergen: Yes, buyers should perform soy-allergen review whenever the ingredient is being approved for a food application or label workflow. The exact label outcome still depends on the jurisdiction, the finished food, and the final reviewer, but the file should not skip source-based allergen assessment.
messages.Yes, for application fit and process con: Yes, for application fit and process consistency. Particle size distribution influences capsule fill-weight uniformity, tablet feeding, blend segregation, dustiness, and handling, so buyers should confirm the method and D-values for the exact grade and format.
messages.Yes, if moisture control is designed del: Yes, if moisture control is designed deliberately — barrier film, desiccant where appropriate, low initial moisture limits, and realistic pack size. Confirm with stability testing on the real finished matrix.
messages.Yes, PS can be evaluated in gummy supple: Yes, PS can be evaluated in gummy supplements, and commercial PS gummy products exist. Feasibility depends on the matrix: the brand must confirm assay recovery, water activity, stability, sensory fit, and dispersion in the actual gummy formula with samples and trials rather than relying on the powder COA alone.
messages.Yes, supported by ingredient origin plus: Yes, supported by ingredient origin plus the manufacturer's allergen control program — but the claim is only as strong as your cross-contact evidence. Keep allergen segregation and cleaning validation records in your substantiation file.
messages.Yes, under conditions. For components ot: Yes, under conditions. For components other than identity of dietary ingredients, 21 CFR 111.75 allows reliance on a supplier COA if the supplier is qualified by confirming the reliability of its COA results, the COA states methods, limits, and actual results, the qualification is documented, and the COA is periodically re-confirmed with quality control review.
messages.Yes, unless an exception applies. CBP's: Yes, unless an exception applies. CBP's marking rules require every foreign-origin article or its container imported into the United States to indicate the English name of the country of origin.
messages.Yes, when the entry line is subject to F: Yes, when the entry line is subject to FSVP. FDA states that the importer must provide its identifying information, including an acceptable UFI, and FDA recognizes the DUNS number for that purpose.
messages.Yes, when the event reveals weak packagi: Yes, when the event reveals weak packaging, route planning, logger control, handoff, carrier qualification, or change communication. Record the trigger and follow the supplier program.
messages.Yes, where the COA supports lot release: Yes, where the COA supports lot release or customer communication. Link the controlled document to the exact lot and version rather than storing an unrelated reference report.

messages.Yes. Buyers should discuss timing early,: Yes. Buyers should discuss timing early, but they should treat document review as part of the real lead-time path. messages.Yes. Clear prior labels, packaging compo: Yes. Clear prior labels, packaging components, documents, and product residues as required by the operating procedure. Label mix-ups can be as significant as ingredient mix-ups.
messages.Yes. Each lot should arrive with a COA r: Yes. Each lot should arrive with a COA reporting the assay, specification version, test basis, and the exact lot number on the drums. Without it, receiving cannot verify the shipment against the PO.
messages.Yes. EU controls use a residue expressio: Yes. EU controls use a residue expression that includes ethylene oxide and 2-chloroethanol expressed as ethylene oxide. A parent-only “not detected” result is incomplete when 2-CE was not measured. Request individual analyte results, reporting limits, and a transparent combined calculation.
messages.Yes. FDA's dietary-supplement labeling g: Yes. FDA's dietary-supplement labeling guidance treats phosphatidylserine as an other dietary ingredient without an established Daily Value, so it should be listed in Supplement Facts with the amount per serving and the no-Daily-Value footnote.
messages.Yes. Include the required form, target m: Yes. Include the required form, target market, application, annual quantity, and document needs so the technical team can match the files to the quoted product.
messages.Yes. It covers all packaging placed on t: Yes. It covers all packaging placed on the EU market, including transport packaging such as 25 kg drums, pallets, and stretch wrap, plus the inner liner and labels. "Placed on the market" means made available for the first time on the EU market in the course of commercial activity.
messages.Yes. Non-preferential origin is part of: Yes. Non-preferential origin is part of the declaration for release for free circulation.
messages.Yes. Ownership, legal entity, contact, e: Yes. Ownership, legal entity, contact, export route, or documentation-system changes can affect traceability and records even when the PS material itself is unchanged.
messages.Yes. Research on capsule filling has sho: Yes. Research on capsule filling has shown that particle size influences fill-weight uniformity and the workable compression range. If D50 or the fines fraction shifts between batches, filling behavior and blend uniformity can change even when assay stays the same.
messages.Yes. Retained samples are commonly sent: Yes. Retained samples are commonly sent to an independent laboratory when a COA needs verification. Keep a documented chain of custody, record the results back to the lot file, and confirm in the quality agreement that the supplier will release retained samples for independent testing when needed.
messages.Yes. Separate files make comparison easi: Yes. Separate files make comparison easier and reduce the risk of mixing source-specific documents in one uncontrolled packet.
messages.Yes. Small quantity does not remove impo: Yes. Small quantity does not remove import-document discipline.
messages.Yes. Source can affect formulation, labe: Yes. Source can affect formulation, labeling, customer acceptance, and document review. Separate the routes even when the finished-product concept is similar.
messages.Yes. Source, allergen, product name, gra: Yes. Source, allergen, product name, grade, storage, and other technical wording should remain consistent with the exact controlled document and finished-product formulation.
messages.Yes. Soy is a major allergen under FALCP: Yes. Soy is a major allergen under FALCPA, and products containing soy-derived PS must declare it. Highly refined lecithin exemptions from some food categories do not automatically carry over to supplement labeling — confirm with regulatory counsel.
messages.Yes. The carrier is part of the ingredie: Yes. The carrier is part of the ingredient and must be declared where labeling rules require component disclosure — relevant for allergen review if the carrier is protein-based. Confirm carrier identity in the spec before finalizing artwork.
messages.Yes. The commercial invoice should carry: Yes. The commercial invoice should carry the country of origin and match the shipment file.
messages.Yes. The Directive applies to all movabl: Yes. The Directive applies to all movable products and does not exclude food. A food supplement containing phosphatidylserine is a product in scope, and the PS ingredient itself is a movable product. What varies by member state is the national transposition, so confirm the rules in force in the destination country.
messages.Yes. The most efficient buyers keep the: Yes. The most efficient buyers keep the sample shipment record, receipt note, and technical outcome together so the tested route can move into quotation and bulk approval without restarting the identity review.
messages.Yes. The public entry requires baseline: Yes. The public entry requires baseline cautionary statements for all products using phosphatidylserine (soy).
messages.Yes. They differ by ingredient source an: Yes. They differ by ingredient source and buyer preference. Use the comparison article and request current specifications before purchasing.
messages.Yes. Those files answer different questi: Yes. Those files answer different questions. Product and market authorization logic should not be used as a substitute for packaging-contact or transport-document review.
messages.Yes. Transaction value remains usable wh: Yes. Transaction value remains usable when the relationship did not influence the price or when the value closely approximates test values for identical or similar merchandise. Document the circumstances of sale and payment chain before entry.
messages.Yes. Under 21 CFR 101.93(a), the manufac: Yes. Under 21 CFR 101.93(a), the manufacturer, packer, or distributor must notify FDA no later than 30 days after first marketing a supplement that bears a structure/function, general well-being, or nutrient-deficiency claim. Notification includes the claim text and a certification that the firm has substantiation; it is a filing, not an approval.
